--- title: "[MixtureCure]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Mixture cure model with logistic incidence and Cox PH latency. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_cure.py#L196-L543){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python MixtureCure(*, emmax=50, eps=1e-07) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The population survival is decomposed as: $$ S_{\text{pop}}(t \mid x, z) = 1 - \pi(x) + \pi(x)\,S_u(t \mid z) $$ where $\pi(x) = \text{expit}(\gamma_0 + \gamma' x)$ is the probability of being susceptible (uncured) and $S_u(t \mid z) = S_0(t)^{\exp(\beta' z)}$ is the latency survival under a Cox proportional hazards model. Parameters are estimated via the EM algorithm. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [emmax]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[50]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of EM iterations (default 50). [eps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-07]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance for the EM algorithm (default 1e-7). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a mixture cure model on the e1684 melanoma dataset: ::: {#8ed03b45 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw e1684 = gw.load_dataset("e1684", backend="polars") # The right-hand side is the latency submodel; `cure=` sets the incidence submodel cure = gw.MixtureCure().fit("Surv(FAILTIME, FAILCENS) ~ TRT", cure=["TRT"], data=e1684) cure ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` MixtureCure (logistic incidence + Cox PH latency) Cure probability model: coef se(coef) z p (Intercept) 1.296 0.2977 4.353 1.34e-05 TRT -0.5747 0.3454 -1.664 0.0961 Failure time distribution model: coef se(coef) z p TRT -0.1318 0.1659 -0.7946 0.427 n = 284, events = 196, EM iterations = 31 ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the mixture cure model via EM.
predict_cure_prob() Predict the probability of being susceptible (uncured).
predict_survival() Predict population survival $S_{\text{pop}}(t \mid x, z)$.
to_frame() Return the summary table as a DataFrame.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the mixture cure model via EM. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_cure.py#L294-L442){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(surv, latency=None, cure=None, *, data=None, nboot=100) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored `Surv` response. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `'Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side sets `latency`. [latency]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariates for the latency (survival) submodel. A dataframe, 2-D array, or formula string evaluated against `data`. A list of column names in `data` also works. [cure]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariates for the incidence (cure) submodel. A dataframe, 2-D array, or formula string evaluated against `data`. A list of column names in `data` also works. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response, `latency`, and `cure`. When `surv` is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. Covariate formula strings and lists of column names are also resolved here. [nboot]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of bootstrap resamples for standard errors (default 100). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [MixtureCure]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a mixture cure model on the `e1684` melanoma dataset. The incidence (cure) submodel and the latency (survival) submodel each receive their own covariates: ::: {#9fe7285d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw e1684 = gw.load_dataset("e1684", backend="polars") # The formula's right-hand side sets `latency` cure = gw.MixtureCure().fit( "Surv(FAILTIME, FAILCENS) ~ TRT", cure=["TRT"], data=e1684 ) cure ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` MixtureCure (logistic incidence + Cox PH latency) Cure probability model: coef se(coef) z p (Intercept) 1.296 0.2977 4.353 1.34e-05 TRT -0.5747 0.3454 -1.664 0.0961 Failure time distribution model: coef se(coef) z p TRT -0.1318 0.1659 -0.7946 0.427 n = 284, events = 196, EM iterations = 31 ``` ::: ::: Inspect the cure-fraction coefficients. A negative intercept in the cure submodel indicates a large estimated cured fraction: ::: {#88de193e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} gw.tidy(cure, format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### [predict_cure_prob()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict the probability of being susceptible (uncured). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_cure.py#L444-L462){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict_cure_prob(cure_covariates, *, data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [cure_covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Covariates for the incidence submodel (same format as `cure` in `fit`). [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : DataFrame for formula evaluation. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of susceptibility probabilities (1 = certainly uncured). ::: ### [predict_survival()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict population survival $S_{\text{pop}}(t \mid x, z)$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_cure.py#L464-L507){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict_survival(times, latency_covariates, cure_covariates, *, data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Time points at which to evaluate survival. [latency_covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Covariates for the latency submodel. [cure_covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Covariates for the incidence submodel. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : DataFrame for formula evaluation. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of shape `(n_subjects, n_times)` with population survival probabilities. ::: ### [to_frame()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the summary table as a DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_cure.py#L509-L543){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python to_frame(*, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Two sections (cure and latency) are stacked, distinguished by a `submodel` column. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns: `submodel`, `term`, `coef`, `se`, `z`, `p`. :::
